title: Parseval identity for mod-2 inner-product characters
statement:
Let $b$ be an arbitrary real-valued function on the set of $n$-bit Boolean inputs. For two such inputs $x,y$, write $\langle x,y\rangle = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i \wedge y_i)$ for the number of coordinates on which both are true, so that $(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}$ is the sign of their mod-2 inner product, equal to $+1$ when $\langle x,y\rangle$ is even and $-1$ when it is odd. Then
\[
  \sum_{x}\Bigl(\sum_{y} b(y)\,(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}\Bigr)^2
  \;=\; 2^n \sum_{y} b(y)^2,
\]
where both the inner and outer sums range over all $n$-bit Boolean inputs.
hypotheses_covered: b is an arbitrary real-valued function on the n-bit Boolean inputs
